title: The Hidden Flaws of SRS: What You Need to Know (SRS Engineering Blog)
description: Candid engineering post from the SRS (Simple Realtime Server) team analyzing the architectural limitations and performance trade-offs of their own RTMP/HLS/WebRTC/SRT media server, including single-process threading constraints and clustering caveats.
reasoning: Primary-source engineering writeup from the maintainers of a major open-source media server, matching this run's vendor/engineering-blog angle. Unusually valuable because it documents real architectural weaknesses rather than marketing claims — exactly the kind of operational detail video engineers need when choosing an ingest server. Fills the under-served RTMP/RTSP/HTTP Protocol Servers gap (14 resources) and sits on the project's own blog domain, not a saturated one.

title: MediaMTX — Zero-Dependency Real-Time Media Server (Official Docs)
description: Official documentation for MediaMTX, a zero-dependency real-time media server and proxy that publishes, reads and converts between RTSP, RTMP, SRT, HLS and WebRTC on a per-path basis. Covers protocol-specific ingest/egress configuration, recording, authentication and the REST control API.
reasoning: Primary-source official docs for one of the most widely deployed modern multi-protocol media servers, and the canonical replacement for nginx-rtmp. The RTMP/RTSP/HTTP Protocol Servers subcategory has only 14 resources and its existing entries are mostly single-protocol Rust/Red5 projects or OBS wiki pages — none document a maintained server that bridges RTSP/RTMP/SRT/WebRTC/HLS in one process. Non-GitHub primary domain, so it also diversifies away from the saturated github.com domain.
